context.firstUser: A streamer, teacher, or group host managing a long contestant roster on a phone, tablet, or desktop while preparing a visible random draw.
context.primaryJob: Confirm the contestant pool, remove mistakes, inspect the full roster, and return to the wheel without losing draw state.
context.desiredResponse: Immediate confidence that every eligible name is present, numbered, manageable, and ready to draw.
referenceProducts: Picker Wheel — editable input list with per-entry actions and long-list tools
Wheel of Names — entry panel separated from the dominant wheel and presentation mode
Classroomscreen — reusable student name lists feeding a randomizer

blurTest.evidence: Across mobile, iPad, and desktop renders, the numbered roster, circular contestant badges, trash actions, and dominant wheel remain recognizable without reading labels.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The producer-list plus live-wheel composition and the roster bottom sheet form a task-specific silhouette rather than a generic dashboard or marketing card stack.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The desktop and iPad first viewport shows Contestant list, the in-pool count, active-pool count, visible names, wheel, and Spin the wheel action simultaneously.

realityTest.evidence: The 24-name test roster contains long, accented, and multi-word names; picked contestants are visibly struck through and labeled as sitting out; the preview caps at 20 and reports four more.

journeyTest.evidence: The same numbering, eligibility state, initials, and trash behavior persist from the 20-row preview into the 24-row sheet; deletion renumbers the remaining pool and Escape returns to the picker.

platformTest.evidence: The mobile sheet uses a bottom-sheet silhouette, 44-point close/delete targets, safe-area-aware footer padding, internal scrolling, body scroll lock, focus placement, and Escape dismissal; desktop keeps the stage within the first 1000-pixel viewport.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The rendered UI is a working roster-management and draw surface with credible data, persistent state, destructive controls, and a full-list inspection path—not a wireframe or promotional mockup.

implementationTest.evidence: The implementation defines a 20-entry preview invariant, a full-list dialog, numbered data contracts, picked/eligible states, focus and keyboard behavior, responsive sticky-stage rules, and geometry assertions for the empty-wheel label.

screenFindings.finding: The zero remains centered in the wheel hub while the explanatory pill sits below it with visible separation; no text is covered.
Compact 56-pixel roster rows preserve numbers, names, picked state, and trash actions while the full pane remains one large open-sheet target.
The full-list sheet exposes total and eligible counts, all contestants through an internal scroll region, explicit picked status, destructive controls, and persistent reset/done actions.
The sticky 790-pixel stage prevents the 20-row producer pane from stretching or displacing the wheel on desktop.
At iPad width, the roster and wheel stay side-by-side with readable controls and the wheel remains fully visible above the fold.
After switching from Spin Wheel to Quick Pick and back, all five wheel segments and labels redraw immediately instead of leaving a blank canvas.
The destructive confirmation clearly identifies the action, affected contestant count, irreversible consequence, and safe Cancel path without clipping on a phone.
The same confirmation remains centered, fully visible, and clearly separates Cancel from the red destructive action on desktop.

repairs: Raised the inline preview cap from five to twenty and added a full-pane click target with a visible View full list affordance.
Added a responsive full-list sheet with eligibility status, delete controls, reset, close, focus placement, Escape handling, safe-area padding, and scroll containment.
Separated the empty-wheel count from its explanatory label so the hub no longer covers the text.
Made the desktop and iPad stage sticky and viewport-sized after the first render showed that twenty inline rows stretched the wheel surface below the initial viewport.
Removed duplicate keyboard targets from the preview affordance so the pane exposes one accessible open action while row trash controls remain independent.
Bound canvas setup and redraw to the active reveal mode so a newly remounted wheel is repainted after returning from Quick Pick.

Added a NameSnap-styled alert dialog to every explicit reset, delete, and clear action, with contextual consequence copy, Cancel focused by default, Escape cancellation, and a distinct destructive confirmation button.
verdict: PASS — the rendered mobile, iPad, and desktop views satisfy the requested 20-name preview, full-list sheet, and empty-wheel text repair without clipping, overlap, or loss of task clarity.
